ranking.notes: Strongest. Scores: beautiful/charismatic 9, French 7, faithful to her text 8, different from Ule 9, works as a reference 9. He is built around the gaze: a calm man who is used to being watched and to owning things, with a half-smile that seduces and appraises at the same time. That half-smile is the direct answer to 'much more charismatic'. Each detail comes from her lines: 'smile rehearsed for Art Basel cameras' and 'the look they use at Sotheby's' (#082), 'the one Jean owes' (#085), and the 'silk lining' turned into clothing. The prompt keeps hands out of the frame and turns the head three-quarters with the face sharp, which suits later edit references. Weak spot: 'French' comes from the words more than from the styling. Lightly polished: added 'rehearsed for cameras' and 'hands out of frame'. 864 characters.

Most French of the three. Scores: beautiful/charismatic 8, French 9, faithful 8, different from Ule 9, reference 7. The ivory silk shirt, oxblood silk lining and loose strand at the brow give a Parisian old-money look. Two risks as written: (1) 'a smile that never reaches his eyes' repeats the coldness of the portrait Elena rejected; (2) a ring on a manicured hand at the lapel invites hand artefacts in a reference image. It also describes nearly the same man as 'charisma' (near-black swept-back hair, olive skin, brown eyes, navy jacket). So the polished pick_b makes him a different man: about 38, tousled collar-length dark chestnut hair, fair skin, dark hazel eyes, a charcoal jacket, a warmer 'dazzling' smile, and hands out of frame.

Most faithful to the 'crack': the drowning man, the debt, and an ultramarine rim light that ties him to #083. Scores: beautiful/charismatic 8, French 7, faithful 9, different from Ule 8, reference 7. Three problems: (1) 'a single thread of silver at the temple' brings back the older look Elena rejected, and Ule's film-9 description already has 'silver only at the temples'; (2) a 'wet brightness' in the eyes can come out tearful, which weakens charisma in a still; (3) warm-plus-ultramarine two-colour lighting changes skin tone, which is worse for a cast reference. Its continuity note is correct for whichever man wins: the 'same pale stone-grey suit in every shot' line and the M1-M5 prompts must change to the new outfit.

pick_a.label: A - The magnetic collector (about 42, sleek near-black hair, olive skin, midnight navy)
pick_a.prompt: Photorealistic chest-up cast reference portrait, 16:9, 35mm film grain, real skin pores, no retouching. An original, non-famous French man of about 42, a very wealthy art collector, strikingly handsome and magnetic: thick near-black hair swept back in a loose natural wave, clean-shaven, light olive skin, aquiline nose, high cheekbones, strong jaw. Heavy-lidded dark brown eyes hold the lens with total calm, a man used to being watched and to owning what he looks at. A slow half-smile, rehearsed for cameras, that seduces and appraises at once. Under the charm, the faintest shadow beneath the eyes: a man who owes. Midnight-navy suit, white shirt open at the throat, no tie, jacket falling open on a dark silk lining. Head turned three-quarters, eyes to camera, hands out of frame. Warm low side light, dark warm-grey background. Face sharp. No text, no logos.
pick_a.plain_english: A sleek, powerful Frenchman of about 42. He has thick near-black hair swept back, olive skin, a strong jaw and an aquiline nose, and he is clean-shaven. His heavy-lidded dark eyes look straight at you, calm, like he already owns the room. His slow half-smile flirts with you and prices you at the same moment (your 'smile rehearsed for Art Basel cameras' and 'the look they use at Sotheby's'). A faint shadow under his eyes hints that he owes someone (#085). He wears a midnight-navy suit with a white shirt open at the neck, no tie, and a dark silk lining showing. He is the opposite of Ule: dark where Ule is blond, smooth where Ule has stubble, brown-eyed where Ule is blue-eyed. Here the charisma is power.

pick_b.label: B - The Parisian charmer (about 38, tousled dark chestnut hair, fair skin, ivory silk)
pick_b.prompt: Photorealistic chest-up cast reference portrait, 16:9, 35mm film grain, real skin pores, no retouching. An original, non-famous Parisian man of about 38, a very rich old-money art collector, beautiful in a dangerous, careless way: dark chestnut hair, tousled and collar-length, one lock falling across the brow; clean-shaven; fair skin; dark straight brows, sculpted cheekbones, narrow straight nose, full mouth. Dark hazel eyes, amused and intimate, hold the lens the way an expert authenticates a canvas. A dazzling smile rehearsed for art-fair cameras that charms you while it prices you; under it, the faint strain of a man who owes. Unstructured charcoal jacket open over an ivory silk shirt unbuttoned at the throat, no tie, a glimpse of oxblood silk lining. Face to camera, hands out of frame. Warm side light, moody umber background. Face sharp. No text, no logos.
pick_b.plain_english: A different man: a younger, more seductive Parisian of about 38 from old money. He has tousled dark chestnut hair to the collar with one lock falling over his brow, fair skin, dark straight brows, sculpted cheekbones and a full mouth. His dark hazel eyes are amused and intimate, and they study you the way an expert checks a painting (your Sotheby's line). He has a dazzling, camera-ready smile that charms you while it prices you, with a faint strain underneath because he owes someone. He wears a soft charcoal jacket over an ivory silk shirt open at the neck, with a flash of deep-red silk lining (your 'voice like silk lining'). He also cannot be mistaken for Ule: chestnut against blond, fair skin against a tan, clean-shaven against stubble, hazel eyes against pale blue. Here the charisma is seduction.

check: Rules confirmed for both picks. (1) Length: A is 864 characters and B is 872, both under 900 (measured with wc -m). (2) Each is an original, non-famous man; neither prompt names a celebrity or a lookalike. (3) No brands, logos or text. Her brand words were turned into images: Hermès became 'silk lining', Sotheby's became 'an expert authenticates/appraises a canvas', Art Basel became 'cameras / art-fair cameras'. Both prompts end with 'No text, no logos'. (4) Each is a photorealistic chest-up reference: 16:9, 35mm grain, real skin pores, face sharp, eyes to camera, hands out of frame (to avoid hand artefacts), with a single warm side light against a dark plain background (no two-colour light, so skin tone stays true). (5) Each is clearly different from Ule (tanned, ash-blond tied back, silver at the temples, golden stubble, pale blue eyes, about 47). Neither is blond, stubbled or blue-eyed, and neither has silver temples. (6) A and B are clearly different men from each other: A is about 42 with sleek near-black hair, olive skin, an aquiline nose, dark brown eyes, a navy suit and a white shirt, and his charm is power. B is about 38 with tousled collar-length dark chestnut hair, fair skin, dark hazel eyes, a charcoal jacket over ivory silk with an oxblood lining, and his charm is seduction. (7) Faithful to her text: the appraising look and Art Basel smile (#082), the proprietor's calm (#082, waist and wrist), and the debt as a faint shadow or strain under the eyes (#085, 'the one Jean owes'). The ages (42 or 38) are our choice, not in her text, as the 50 was before.
